data.title: Treasury Yields At Multi-Year Highs Ahead of Expected Fed Hike — Market Talk
data.description:
1546 ET - Treasury yields settle at new multi-year highs as markets price a Fed hike while facing an uncertain long-term outlook. Inflation expectations hover around 2.5%, as measured by one-year swap rates, according to LSEG, higher than the Fed's 2% target. That's up from below-target expectations in early August. A 20-year Treasury auction clears at the highest yield since 1986, shortly before the tenor was discontinued, and since it was reintroduced in 2020. Demand indicators in the sale come on the soft side. The 10-year yield rises 0.035 percentage point to 4.995%, the highest since July 2007. The two-year adds 0.028 points to 4.661%, highest since July 2024. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1537 ET - The WSJ Dollar Index rises 0.2%, as the currency keeps tracking U.S. Treasury yields. Bonds sell off as investors face uncertainty regarding government debt, inflation and increasing debt supply. The Fed is expected to raise rates tomorrow, while great weight is put on post-meeting communication. "A higher dot plot and clear willingness to tighten again would support the dollar, while a cautious signal, or a 'dovish hike' market read could trigger a reversal," Convera's Kevin Ford said in an email. The dollar strengthens 0.5% versus the yen and is flat against the euro. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1526 ET - Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D., NY) voted no on a measure to advance the Clarity Act, a piece of legislation backed by President Trump that would boost the cryptocurrency industry. The measure was ultimately defeated 49 to 50. Gillibrand was the Democrat that Republican Sen. Cynthia Lummis (Wyo.) has been leaning on in her arguments that the bill had bipartisan support. The senators introduced legislation together in 2022 to try to establish a framework for digital assets. Lummis praised Gillibrand at a conference on Friday for her work in pushing the Clarity Act forward. Ahead of Gillibrand's no vote, her Democratic colleague Sen. Elizabeth Warren voiced concerns that the bill lacked adequate safeguards against corruption in the light of President Trump's deep financial ties to the crypto industry. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1430 ET - Treasury yields tick higher as investors demand steeper returns to lend money to Washington long-term. A 20-year Treasury bond auction clears at a yield of 5.42%, the highest since 1986, when the tenor was discontinued, and since it was reintroduced in 2020. Still, demand indicators were on the soft side: the 2.57 bid-to-cover ratio was below the previous six-month average of 2.65, while indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign investors, took 52.5% of the bonds, also below average. The 20-year trades at 5.414%, up from 5.401% before the auction, while the 10-year rises to 5.014% from 4.996%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1429 ET - Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says he will meet with China's Vice Premier He Lifeng this weekend to continue discussing sanctions on Iran. "We have sanctioned three banks with China," Bessent says. "We have had some very good private discussions, and I look forward to those continuing this weekend when I meet my Chinese counterpart," he tells the House Financial Services Committee during a hearing. (jessica.coacci@wsj.com)

1311 ET - Rising bond yields beat out the prospect of an AI bubble as the biggest "tail risk," according to the latest Bank of America survey of global fund managers. About one-third of survey respondents named a "disorderly rise in bond yields" as the biggest tail risk, while 28% named an AI bubble, down from 32% in August. Bond yields have been climbing, fueled by surging energy prices brought on by the Iran war and growing national debt among other factors. The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.04% earlier, its highest level since 2007. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1310 ET - The AI data center boom is expected to keep chugging along, according to Bank of America's latest survey of global fund managers. Of those surveyed, 79% said they do not expect one of the AI hyperscalers to announce a cut in capital expenditures this year, up from 71% in August. But investors see the spending as carrying some risk: 42% of respondents named AI hyperscaler capex as the most likely source of a systemic credit event, and net 33% said companies are overinvesting. As for the most crowded trade, 53% identified "long global semiconductors" which matched last month's survey. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1203 ET - Investors are increasingly expecting global interest rates to rise, according to findings from Bank of America's September survey of global fund managers. 41% of surveyed investors said they expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates before the U.S. midterms, up from 22% in August, while the proportion of investors who don't expect a rate hike fell to 52% from 72%. A net 32% of investors expect higher short-term rates, and net 25% said global monetary policy is too stimulative - with both metrics at their highest level since September 2022. Net 4% of investors expect lower global inflation, a reversal from the previous month. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1133 ET - Bitcoin's price is under pressure from both long-term investors and short-term traders rushing to sell and lock in their profits, analysts with Glassnode say in a note. The cryptocurrency has bounced up to trade near a 47% premium to the average price that traders paid for it, meaning most sales are profitable right now, the analysts say. Long-term and short-term holders seem to be cashing out in roughly equal amounts, they say. But the shift toward profit-taking matches behavior seen during other price surges in recent years, signaling that the latest rally hasn't peaked or collapsed yet, the analysts say. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1110 ET - The Iran war is creating sharply different fiscal outcomes across the Gulf depending on countries' ability to keep hydrocarbons flowing, Capital Economics says. Higher energy prices are more than offsetting limited export disruption in the U.A.E. and Oman, improving their budget balances this year. By contrast, budget balances are expected to deteriorate by around 2% of GDP in Saudi Arabia, around 5% in Kuwait and Bahrain, and as much as 10% in Qatar compared with last year. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1059 ET - Bitcoin's recent pullback from the $79,000 level reflects continued uncertainty among investors ahead of the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting rather than a bearish trend reversal, XS.com's Simon-Peter Massabni says in a note. The cryptocurrency's price action of late highlights a clash between buyers trying to defend current levels and sellers concerned by a stronger U.S. dollar and rising interest rate expectations, Massabni says. "The Federal Reserve remains the most influential factor in Bitcoin's short-term outlook," he says. The central bank's interest rate decision is important, but so is the messaging that policymakers are sending about the future of monetary policy, Massabni says. Bitcoin is down 3% at $75,940, according to data from CoinGlass. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1049 ET - Investors should focus on the vote split at the Bank of England rate decision on Thursday for a signal on the possibility of a BOE interest-rate increases in future months, Peel Hunt's Kallum Pickering says in a note. Additionally, communication by monetary policy committee members could provide clues, he says. If BOE Governor Andrew Bailey doubles down on his comments about second-round inflation effects being subdued, this could lower expectations of BOE rate increases, Pickering says. However, if the governor indicates higher inflation expectations then markets will see that as an endorsement of current market pricing, he says. Investors fully price in a total of four BOE rate increases by mid-2027, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

data.title: Retailers Report Miyoko's Creamery Vegan Butter Recall Due to Risk of E. Coli
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

A Miyoko's Creamery vegan butter product is being recalled due to concerns about potential E. coli, according to notices posted by multiple retailers.

Sprouts Farmers Market said the recall includes 8-ounce packages of European-style salted plant milk butter with UPC number 857554005773 and lot number 1007871. The product is made from cashew milk.

Miyoko's is part of Boise, Idaho-based Prosperity Organic Foods, which also owns vegan butter business Melt Organic.

Wegmans, Natural Grocers and Raley's also posted recall notices. A recall notice from earlier in September said microbiological results didn't meet quality standards.

data.title: Futures Recover as Russia, Ukraine Exchange Strikes — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery rose 0.9% Tuesday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $7.28 1/2 a bushel as winter planting got off to a slow start and optimism faded for a Russia-Ukraine truce.
  • Soybeans for November delivery rose 1.1% to $13.18 3/4 a bushel.
  • Corn for December delivery rose 0.5% to $5.35 3/4 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Hopes Dashed: Grain futures shook off early weakness as expectations dimmed for a truce between Russia and Ukraine after the two sides exchanged strikes overnight despite President Trump's assertion that they had agreed to stop attacks on energy targets. The prospect of such a halt prompted hopes that any agreement could extend to attacks on shipping in the Black Sea, which has affected grain exports.

Crop Progress: The U.S. corn crop was in 57% good/excellent condition this week, up from 56% the week before but down from 67% this time last year, according to the USDA's latest report. The corn harvest was 8% complete compared with 7% a year ago. "The widespread heat waves seen to finish the growing season have certainly sped up maturity, but scattered heavy rains across the Midwest in the last week ultimately kept somewhat of a lid on progress at the national level," Mike Castle of StoneX said in a note. Soybeans were 58% good/excellent, with 6% harvested. That's double the five-year average of 3%, "again reflecting the rapid maturation due to recent excessive heat," Castle said.

INSIGHT

Behind on Planting: U.S. winter wheat planting at 8% is below the five-year average of 12% for this time of year, which raises concerns about a second consecutive year of low winter wheat production, analysts at Rabobank said in a note. On the bearish side, global inventories are rising amid logistics constraints, and increasing stocks in Ukraine and Russia "could lead to a substantial carryover into the next marketing year," they added.

Ethanol Exports: The U.S. exported a record 2.2 billion gallons of ethanol in 2025 worth $4.7 billion, and exports of the biofuel were up 12% in the first half of this year by volume and 21% by value, the USDA said in a report, noting growing global demand and reduced competition from Brazil. Several unknowns could alter the trajectory. Brazil may recover export market share if its production outpaces domestic consumption growth, while any change in U.S. policy, such as a nationwide E15 mandate, could limit exportable supply and push up prices. Demand may also rise further as countries respond to higher energy prices caused by the Middle East conflict. "Ethanol prices have not spiked like oil and gasoline, giving ethanol an advantage and encouraging higher blending as a method to reduce prices at the pump," the USDA said.

AHEAD

  • The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
  • The USDA will release its monthly Cattle on Feed report at 3 p.m. ET Friday.
  • The CFTC will release its weekly Commitment of Traders report at 3:30 p.m. ET Friday.

Write to Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: CBOT corn futures climb, following strength in soy, wheat and crude oil
data.description:

data.title: LatAm stocks, FX mixed as oil and bond yields weigh; fiscal worries hit Colombia
data.description:
Key points:
  • LatAm FX up 0.2%, stocks up 0.2%
  • Brazil retail sales fall more than expected in July
  • Lula would beat Bolsonaro in a Brazilian runoff, predicts CNT/MDA poll
  • Colombia Congress approves 2027 budget as fiscal strains deepen
  • US Fed, Brazil cenbank rate decisions due Wednesday

By Avinash P and Ragini Mathur

Latin American stocks and currencies were mixed on Tuesday as surging oil prices and rising global bond yields kept investor sentiment in check, while Colombian assets fell after the country's Congress approved the 2027 budget.

MSCI's index tracking LatAm stocks (.MILA00000PUS) gained 0.2%, while a corresponding currencies gauge (.MILA00000CUS) also rose 0.2%, with both indexes stabilizing after the previous session's selloff.

Colombia's Congress on Monday approved the government's 2027 spending budget of 634.9 trillion pesos ($206.6 billion), as a sharp deterioration in public finances is expected to push the fiscal deficit to a record high next year.

President Abelardo De La Espriella's government plans to submit a tax reform package, known as the "Rescue Law," and pursue spending cuts next year in an effort to reduce the fiscal deficit to 7.2% of gross domestic product, Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said.

"We would also expect the government to continue pursuing executive actions next year to improve fiscal results," Citi analysts said in a note, adding that the key issue for the markets would be the "eventual magnitude and permanence of the expenditure savings."

Colombian stocks fell 0.9%, while the peso weakened 0.2%.

Political developments remained in focus in Brazil, with a CNT/MDA poll released on Tuesday showing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva would defeat right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a second-round runoff in next month's election.

The survey added to a string of polls pointing to a tight presidential race ahead of the October vote. Markets have been closely watching shifts in political sentiment, with analysts viewing Bolsonaro as the more market-friendly candidate.

Brazil's benchmark Bovespa stock index rose 0.8%, recovering after a 0.9% decline on Monday, while the real was little changed.

Brazilian retail sales fell more than expected in July, highlighting the strain that high borrowing costs are placing on consumer spending.

"High borrowing costs are weighing most heavily on discretionary and durable purchases, while resilient employment and real-income growth continue to provide some support to essential spending," said Andrés Abadía, chief Latin America economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

Attention will now turn to the central bank's monetary policy committee, known as Copom, which is expected to cut its benchmark interest rate to 13.75% from 14.00% on Wednesday.

Elsewhere, oil prices extended their rally after attacks on energy infrastructure in the Gulf heightened supply concerns.

Higher energy prices have supported assets in the region's net oil-exporting countries, though sustained strength in crude has also fueled inflation concerns and pushed global bond yields to multi-year highs, pressuring emerging markets as a whole.

The Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday remains the key event for global markets. The U.S. central bank is widely expected to raise rates by at least 25 basis points, compared with an even split between a hike and a pause just a week ago.

In Peru, the economy expanded 3.56% in July from a year earlier, beating expectations as strong growth in construction, trade and services offset weakness in manufacturing, agriculture and fishing.

The Peruvian sol eased 0.3%, while the country's stocks (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) were flat.

data.title: Qualcomm Stock Jumps. Amazon AI Chip Deal Opens New Growth Avenue
data.description:
Qualcomm QCOM stock jumped 5% on Tuesday after receiving fresh attention from StoneX, as its expansion into data-center chips gives investors another potential growth avenue beyond smartphones.

StoneX analyst Cody Acree kept a Buy rating and $270 price target on Qualcomm. The view follows the company's recent collaboration with Amazon on customized AI silicon and high-speed optical connectivity for data centers.

Qualcomm expects its data-center business to generate about $5 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue and more than $15 billion by fiscal 2029. The company also projects total non-handset revenue of $40 billion by fiscal 2029 as it expands across automotive, IoT and other markets.

The diversification comes as Qualcomm's handset business faces pressure. Fiscal third-quarter handset revenue fell 20% year over year to $5.09 billion, according to company data cited by analysts. Acree expects non-handset operations to become a larger contributor to Qualcomm's semiconductor business, shifting investor focus toward execution in newer markets.

Investors are now focused on Wednesday's Fed decision. Market pricing points to a quarter-point increase, which would mark the first rate hike since 2023. The move comes as policymakers face renewed inflation pressure from energy prices and elevated borrowing costs.

data.title: UMG sues DistroKid for allegedly distributing AI 'slop' music
data.description:
By Blake Brittain

Universal Music Group sued DistroKid in Delaware federal court on Tuesday, accusing the online music distributor of infringing the label's copyrights and "flooding platforms with AI-generated 'slop' that siphons revenue and listeners from the legitimate artists."

The lawsuit accused DistroKid of bolstering its streaming numbers and revenue with mass-uploaded, bot-generated "spam" music as well as "thousands" of unlicensed versions of UMG recordings.

"At scale, DistroKid’s conduct makes it more difficult for working and emerging artists to be discovered and compensated for their creative labor," the complaint said.

Spokespeople for DistroKid did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.

DistroKid is a distribution service that allows recording artists to upload music across online stores and streaming platforms. Spotify, which is not named in the lawsuit, bought a minority stake in the company in 2018.

UMG's lawsuit said that a "massive portion" of DistroKid's music is either AI "slop" or copyright-infringing despite the distributor's assurances otherwise. In addition to alleged AI "slop," the label accused DistroKid of releasing thousands of tracks that are "remixed or speed-altered" UMG recordings, illegally sample UMG music, or otherwise violate its rights.

UMG said DistroKid violated its rights in at least 1,000 recordings by popular artists including, The Beatles, Drake, Lady Gaga and Rihanna. It asked the court for monetary damages and an order blocking DistroKid's alleged misconduct.

The complaint also said that DistroKid created many of its AI tracks using the AI music generator Suno. UMG has separately sued Suno for allegedly misusing its music for AI training.

The case is UMG Recordings Inc v. DistroKid LLC, U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01156.

For UMG: Glenn Pomerantz of Munger, Tolles & Olson

For DistroKid: attorney information not yet available

data.title: Spuds Powell: 6 Wealth Management Lessons Learned Over 3 Decades — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Greg Bartalos

Spuds Powell is worth listening to. The Kayne Anderson Rudnick managing director is ranked No. 3 in Barron's 2026 Top 100 Independent Advisors list, maintaining a Top 10 position in the ranking for 14 consecutive years. Inducted into the Barron's Hall of Fame in 2022, Powell also serves on the firm's Wealth Advisory Investment Committee and previously held roles at Financial Engines and Franklin Templeton.

Earlier this year, Powell contributed a well-received guest column for Barron's Advisor, headlined What Clients Have Taught Me: 6 Reflections From a Career in Wealth Management. "After more than three decades advising individuals and families, I've come to believe that wealth management is equal parts technical skill and human connection," he writes. "But the deepest lessons-the ones that have shaped me as an advisor and as a person-have come from the relationships I have built along the way."

Powell joined Barron's Advisor's The Way Forward podcast, where he drills deeper into each of the six points, sharing common sense, counterintuitive advice, and colorful anecdotes, with the throughline being that "connection is the real currency."

In his article, Powell explains why constructive criticism can be "a gift." On the podcast, he elaborates, saying "there will be many times where clients express dissatisfaction or constructive criticism or suggestions for improvement, and it's important at those times to be on receive mode, as my dad used to say, and to be open-minded to their feedback rather than being defensive and trying to push back...I could think of two clients in particular that over the years have been very demanding. They've had extremely high expectations for me personally as their wealth advisor for our firm, but they've always had very reasonable requests. And thanks to them, I personally have become a much better wealth advisor."

Powell also writes that trust isn't only established during major life events. "Lighthearted moments build relationships," too. On the podcast, he recounts with a natural storyteller's flair a tale about a client who was clearly comfortable working with him and committed to the relationship. "One longtime client couple staged a prank on me when we met at a diner, conspiring with our waitress to have her pretend to recognize me from my college football days. I believed every word until they couldn't keep straight faces any longer."

Read all of Powell's lessons here and listen to the podcast (and read the transcript) here.

data.title: Nvidia could ride a $3.2 trillion semiconductor boom
data.description:
Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials), the leader in AI accelerators, might be in a semiconductor market that is much earlier in its boom phase than investors believe.

Bank of America estimates that the industry's total addressable market will be $3.2 trillion by 2030, almost doubling as demand permeates memory, data centers and other important semiconductor areas. That's a stunning amount, the forecast says.

The semiconductor industry takes almost 50 years to get to $1 trillion in yearly sales. AI infrastructure is accelerating the next phase of growth.

Data centers are still an important part of that picture, giving Nvidia exposure to one of the greatest areas for investing in the sector. But Bank of America thinks the opportunity might be bigger.

Strong demand for memory and potential recovery in the automotive and industrial semiconductor industries. Spending on server, PC, smartphone and semiconductor equipment also all projected to climb through 2030.

As for the broader semiconductor momentum weakness, the bank cited Nvidia and AMD as resilient compute names. Networking saw Marvell in the spotlight, while among analog names were Analog Devices and onsemi.

The $3.2 trillion projection casts the current AI boom in a new light for investors in Nvidia.

The next question is whether AI infrastructure spending can be robust enough to turn that giant industry projection into continuous revenue growth.

data.title: Treasuries Move Back To The Downside Ahead Of Fed Announcement
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After recovering from early weakness to end the previous session modestly higher, treasuries moved back to the downside during trading on Tuesday.

Bond prices came under pressure early in the session and remained firmly negative throughout the day. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, advanced 3.5 basis points to 4.996 percent.

The ten-year yield climbed as high as 5.016 percent during the day, marking its highest level since July 2007.

The weakness among treasuries came amid concerns about the outlook for inflation and interest rates ahead of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision on Wednesday.

The Fed is widely expected to raise interest rates, with CME Group's FedWatch Tool currently indicating a 94.5 percent chance of a quarter point rate hike.

'A 25bp Fed hike is now almost fully priced, meaning the bigger catalyst will be whether Kevin Warsh presents it as a one-off recalibration or signals that persistent inflation requires further tightening,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com

A sharp increase by the price of crude oil also weighed on treasuries, with U.S. crude oil futures spiking by more than 4 percent.

Supply concerns continue to drive the price of crude oil higher amid reports of fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia.

data.description: The prospect of slowing or pausing AI development doesn't herald any change to the fundamentals of the AI infrastructure buildout, Morgan Stanley co-president Dan Simkowitz says in a CNBC interview. "I think the pause or the slowing of release on the frontier really doesn't change the core dynamics," Simkowitz says, adding that spending on computing power and semiconductors doesn't show any signs of stopping. "The pacing at the frontier doesn't change the build, it doesn't change the demand, and it doesn't change the financing of that demand." He adds that capital markets remain ready for large M&A activity and IPOs. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

data.title: Bitcoin Falls as Clarity Act Fails to Advance. Why Cathie Wood's Dumping Crypto Stocks. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Callum Keown

It's crunch time for cryptocurrencies.

The Senate will vote on the Clarity Act, a key bill for crypto regulation, on Tuesday afternoon.

Bitcoin and crypto-exposed stocks were falling ahead of the vote, though, after enjoying a rally in recent months as the legislation's chances of being passed have come back from the dead.

It's still a tight call. GOP senators have been making an 11th-hour push to get support from Democrats, Barron's reported Monday. But the odds of the bill passing this year slipped to 19% Tuesday from 31% yesterday, according to prediction market Polymarket. Polymarket has a data sharing partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of Barron's.

That move, and broader pre-vote nerves are being reflected in crypto markets. Bitcoin fell to $76,408 early in the day, down 2.7% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinDesk data. The world's largest cryptocurrency is up 31% since the start of July but remains 12% down in 2026.

Ethereum, the second largest crypto, slipped 3.2% to $2,427, while popular altcoin XRP edged 0.5% lower to $1.40.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest took the opportunity to sell crypto-related stocks Monday, according to a trading notification. ARK's funds sold shares in CoinDesk owner Bullish, crypto exchange Coinbase, stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group, and Ethereum treasury company Bitmine Immersion Technologies.

Coinbase stock was down 5.6% in early trading, after rallying 9% in the previous session. Strategy, the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, was down 3% after a 4.6% rise Monday.

data.title: This Energy Stock Proves That AI Data Center Demand Is Still Surging — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Artificial intelligence may have triggered doomsday fears about humanity's future, but one rising energy player is showing that demand for data-center infrastructure isn't slowing down.

Shares of Forgent Power Solutions, an electrical-distribution equipment maker, jumped 11% to $31.81 on Tuesday after the company reported strong earnings before the market open.

Management attributed the better-than-expected results to the surging demand for AI data-center equipment. Forgent Power makes modular power systems, or flexible energy distribution hubs that manage and deliver uninterrupted power to servers, that are used specifically for data-center buildouts. Sales for its modular power systems grew 296% from a year ago in fiscal 2026.

Forgent's revenue soared 94% to $461.7 million in the fiscal fourth quarter ended in June, beating analysts' calls for $429.9 million. Adjusted earnings totaled 25 cents a share, just edging out estimates of 24 cents, according to FactSet.

CEO Gary Niederpruem said in a statement that Forgent's earnings surpassed the expectations set when the company first went public on Feb. 5. Customers are relying on to Forgent to execute "unprecedented build-outs" to meet the growing AI demand, he said.

A 375% surge in orders alongside a book-to-bill ratio of 3.3-meaning Forgent received $3.30 in new orders for every $1 of product it shipped-reflected massive buying activity and a strong appetite for Forgent's equipment in the fiscal fourth quarter. With an order backlog of $3 billion, customers have pre-ordered electrical equipment years in advance to lock in power delivery for data-center expansions.

To handle those order backlogs, Forgent said it will invest $25 million to expand production lines at its Tijuana campus, increasing total revenue capacity to $5.8 billion by late fiscal 2027.

Forgent said it expects adjusted earnings between $1.26 and $1.40 a share on revenue between $2.4 billion and $2.6 billion for fiscal 2027-"significantly higher than the company's IPO forecast.' Analysts project adjusted earnings of $1.13 a share on revenue of $2.09 billion.

data.title: Dollar Outlook Hinges on Fed Communication — Market Talk
data.description: The WSJ Dollar Index rises 0.2%, as the currency keeps tracking U.S. Treasury yields. Bonds sell off as investors face uncertainty regarding government debt, inflation and increasing debt supply. The Fed is expected to raise rates tomorrow, while great weight is put on post-meeting communication. "A higher dot plot and clear willingness to tighten again would support the dollar, while a cautious signal, or a 'dovish hike' market read could trigger a reversal," Convera's Kevin Ford said in an email. The dollar strengthens 0.5% versus the yen and is flat against the euro. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)
